content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware geocoding and spatial modelling link partially located farm policies to hail exposure and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments more reliably than municipality-level loading? A first experiment would mask known farm locations to test address reconstruction and uncertainty calibration, then test loss prediction on held-out storms or years to assess whether the available weather data support finer-scale estimates.

rationale.text: Pejić has developed hierarchical geographic imputation methods for partially geocoded Vojvodina records, directly relevant to policies located only at settlement level.

sources.quote: This paper develops a sequential MI procedure that first draws a settlement conditional on municipality using population-weighted multinomial sampling
Compared to single-imputation alternatives, the MI approach produced correctly calibrated confidence intervals for tract-level rate estimates

rationale.text: He has evaluated Serbian address-geocoding methods against field-verified coordinates, including rural positional error.

sources.quote: The ensemble approach also produced positional accuracy estimates; median offset from field-verified coordinates was 148 m for urban addresses and 540 m for rural addresses.

rationale.text: His methodological work includes masked-location validation and comparisons of spatial estimation methods, providing a relevant experimental approach rather than an assumption that one model will transfer.

sources.quote: A random 30% of geocoded cases were masked to simulate the incomplete-geocoding scenario.
Predictive performance was evaluated by mean absolute error and interval coverage at tract level.

rationale.text: He has previously adapted registry spatial methods to administrative insurance claims with incomplete addresses, although in health rather than agricultural insurance.

sources.quote: adapting registry-based spatial smoothing approaches to the fund's incomplete address fields.

constraints.text: Location uncertainty and weather resolution must remain explicit: settlement-only addresses and daily five-kilometre weather grids cannot be treated as observed field-level hail intensity.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: The initial study must fit the stated three-year, approximately 1,200-policy loss dataset and establish whether its real coordinates provide suitable validation cases.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.
He has expressed preference for partners who can supply real address or location data for validation work rather than purely synthetic datasets.

constraints.text: Any operational output must have an agreed automated interface to the existing Python pricing workflow; manual mapping alone does not meet the task.

sources.quote: Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh
turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.

constraints.text: Scope and engineering ownership must accommodate limited company development capacity and Pejić's restricted capacity for large commitments before mid-2027.

sources.quote: a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.
which limits capacity for large new commitments before mid-2027.

risks: The demonstrated methods concern residential health records and relatively smooth incidence surfaces, not farm parcels or narrow hail tracks. Population-weighted imputation and spatial smoothing could misplace agricultural exposure or erase storm boundaries; the first experiment must test this transfer explicitly.

Daily five-kilometre weather data may contain insufficient information for field-level hail reconstruction, regardless of geocoding quality. Access to finer weather observations or independent hail validation is unknown.
Three claim years may contain too few independent hail events for reliable validation. Geo-tagged claimants may also differ systematically from incompletely located policies.
Losses above pricing assumptions do not establish that spatial exposure is the cause; asset values, coverage, deductibles and repair-cost changes could explain part of the difference.
An R-based research prototype could remain unintegrated without company engineering ownership; the company's earlier flood-mapping prototype was not integrated into pricing.
Pejić's actual availability, willingness to apply his methods outside health, project funding, data-access permissions and delivery schedule remain unconfirmed.
questions: Will Pejić confirm interest in a bounded agricultural-insurance joint project, and what time and team capacity can he commit before and after mid-2027?
Are coordinates available for insured fields and buildings, or only residences and claim locations? Can parcel boundaries and verified locations be obtained for an independent validation sample?
Can the company provide the complete insured portfolio, including non-claiming policies, coverage periods, insured values, deductibles, premiums, claim dates and loss amounts?
Which MeteoVoj variables actually measure or proxy hail, how were they validated, and are radar, storm-track or finer-resolution observations available and licensed for pricing use?
Can validation hold out entire storms or years, and what minimum predictive improvement, uncertainty calibration and usable spatial resolution would justify proceeding beyond the pilot?
Who will own the Python integration and maintenance, what budget and timeline are available, and what explanations and approval process are required before changing rating factors?
What data-sharing, access-control, retention and insurance-pricing requirements apply to policyholder locations and loss records?
